name: Amazon DocumentDB
model: MongoDB-compatible API (3.6, 4.0, 5.0, 8.0 levels) over JSON-like documents in collections; not MongoDB's own code
engine_note: AWS-built engine on Aurora-style shared storage: one cluster volume, six copies over three AZs, separate compute instances
consistency: Single-document writes atomic; multi-document transactions (4.0+) use snapshot isolation. Every write waits for 4 of 6 storage copies (cannot be lowered). Primary reads are read-after-write; replica reads are eventually consistent (usually under 100 ms lag).
scaling: One writer plus up to 15 read replicas sharing storage that grows to 256 TiB; Elastic Clusters shard collections for more write throughput.
version_note: Engine 8.0 (MongoDB 8.0 compatibility) generally available 2025-11-14; 8.0.2 release notes dated 2026-09-28.
reach: Reach for it when you are on AWS, have code written for the MongoDB API, and want AWS to run it with durable shared storage and read replicas.
avoid: Avoid when you need full MongoDB feature parity (some operators and features are missing) or want to run the same database outside AWS.
escape: You want MongoDB-style documents run by AWS with storage-level durability, not Postgres rows.
chat: Chats stored as documents for a team already on the MongoDB API and on AWS; otherwise not needed.
notes: Do not confuse with the separate open source 'DocumentDB' project: a MongoDB-compatible document database built as PostgreSQL extensions, started by Microsoft in 2024, MIT licensed, which joined the Linux Foundation on 2025-08-25 (AWS said it would contribute to it). Sources: https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-welcomes-documentdb-to-advance-open-developer-first-nosql-innovation and https://github.com/documentdb/documentdb. Amazon DocumentDB's own engine is closed; AWS docs do not describe the on-disk data structure, so engine is 'other'. Transactions: one minute execution limit; linearizable read concern not supported. Volume limit 256 TiB is for engine 8.0+ (128 TiB earlier). No Jepsen report.
